summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT A SEMANTIC TEST. fixed_parent_lexicon.denotation: An agent desires the following purpose or predicate; no achievement entailed.
Drying is the intended medical purpose, not a successful physiological effect.
One compound noun phrase: belly characterized as moist.
Introduces the observation guard; does not assert its satisfaction in an actual patient or cook.
Composite observation predicate on the current food after the first boiling stage. No exact time, temperature or objective degree is measured.
Pour away the selected water; does not silently remove the food or every liquid belonging to it.
Select the former member W0 of this preparation’s water sequence. Its noun argument is position9 across position8.
One composite transfer predicate with an immediacy modifier; its food argument is supplied by the declared topic binding. Immediacy does not prove zero air exposure.
The same water kind at9 and12. FIRST/OTHER create distinct contextual water references; the word itself does not change meaning.
Same IN relation in transfer postcondition and the reboil location; no TO-versus-IN word polysemy.
Introduces W1 distinct from previously selected W0, with the same water kind.

Generic liquid kind. Apposition in C01 resolves it to W1; OWN in C03 and the inherited owner schema in C04/C05 resolve it to the food’s intrinsic juice. This context narrowing is an explicit grammar cost, not a fixed JUICE gloss.
HOT(W1), no numeric temperature or patient state.
Resumes the W1 introduced by OTHER WATER, not W0.
Composite AGAIN + thorough BOIL. Introduces a second boiling event, distinct from the first moderately boiled appearance. Its internal three-part content is counted as a lexical cost.
SOFT is the instructed endpoint; UNTIL does not guarantee eventual reachability.
Same kind at19/38: the current cooked portion at19, a variable of that same kind under NO at38. A new generic binder, not a switch to all objects.
Softness endpoint of the same food; not successful drying or evacuation.
Same relation to a use/purpose at21,29,46. C02 norm, C03 reason and C05 relevance scopes are declared by productions; FOR does not itself create a medical effect.
Same evacuation goal at22/47, resumed by THIS_USE30.
One boiling operation in the C02 prohibition, C03 quoted reprise and C05 duration comparison. Occurrence mode comes from the production, not a new word meaning.
In C02 negates permission for FULLY(BOIL), not all boiling, not the evacuation goal and not the retention desire.

One completion modifier: BOIL has a thorough-preparation endpoint; RETAIN has complete own-juice retention. These two chosen endpoint interpretations are explicit semantic assumptions, not a shared numerical scale.
C03 takes the previously prohibited FULLY BOIL as quoted explanandum and the retention desire as reason.
Resumes the evacuation purpose of C02; no unmarked return to the drying branch.
Same denotation as porain; freely assumed whole-word synonym, counted.
Retain the food’s own intrinsic liquid/juice. Under DESIRE/AS_POSSIBLE this is a goal, not an observed achieved amount.
Qualify the desired extent as as much/as fully as feasible. No numerical optimum, attained maximum or existence of a maximizing physical state is asserted.
Select the food’s intrinsic juice, J(owner), rather than the cooking water merely surrounding that owner.
No member of the stated cooked-food kind can satisfy the following complete-retention capability.
Capability to retain at a given extent. It is not an alias of the DESIRE-governed RETAIN verb at32; final COMPLETELY supplies its extent argument.
Same completion extent as FULLY when applied to retention. Its scope is the embedded retention extent of CAN_RETAIN, not completion of an ability itself. This is one freely assumed lexical synonym.
Compare longer with shorter relevant histories; no minutes or universal unbounded continuous-time law.
Greater own-juice loss in the corresponding history; no fraction or invented measured amount.
Loss of own juice during boiling; the word does not encode a clinical effect.
Connect the final loss comparison to the earlier evacuation policy/rationale; it is not a newly executed cooking step.

section.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ φακῆν ἔφαμεν ὁμοίωϲ κράμβη χρῆναι ϲκευάζειν, ἀμφότερα καὶ αὐτὴν ἐργάζεϲθαι δυναμένην, ὑπαγωγήν τε καὶ ϲτάλϲιν γαϲτρόϲ. ὀνομάζεται δ’ ἡ οὕτωϲ ϲκευαϲθεῖϲα δίϲεφθοϲ καὶ κράμβη καὶ φακῆ. καὶ κρόμυον δὲ καὶ πράϲον καὶ πολὺ μᾶλλον ἀμπελόπραϲόν τε καὶ ϲκόροδον, ὅ τι τ’ ἂν ἄλλο βουληθῇϲ ἐπὶ τοὐναντίον ἀποϲτῆϲαι τῆϲ ἀρχαίαϲ φύϲεωϲ, οὕτω ϲκεύαζε μεμνημένοϲ ἐκείνου πρὸ πάντων. ὡϲ οὐ χρὴ ψαύειν οὔτ’ ἀέροϲ οὔθ’ ὕδατοϲ ψυχροῦ τὸ δὶϲ ἑψόμενον· οὐκέτι γὰρ ἀκριβῶϲ γίγνεται τακερόν, οὐδ’ ἂν ἐπὶ πλεῖϲτον ἕψῃϲ, ἀλλὰ χρή, καθάπερ εἶπον ἀρτίωϲ, ἕτοιμον ἔχονταϲ ὕδωρ θερμόν, ἀνελκύϲανταϲ ἐκ τοῦ προτέρου μεταβάλλειν εὐθέωϲ εἰϲ ἐκεῖνο.
section.english_working_translation: Indeed, we also said that lentil soup should be prepared like cabbage, since it too can bring about both evacuation and checking of the belly. Both cabbage and lentil soup prepared in this way are called twice-boiled. Prepare onion and leek too, and much more wild leek and garlic, and whatever else you wish to change toward the opposite of its original nature, in this way, remembering this above all: the thing being twice boiled must touch neither air nor cold water. For it no longer becomes properly soft, even if you boil it for a very long time. Rather, as I have just said, have hot water ready, draw it from the former water and immediately transfer it into that.
section.translation_status: Own source-side semantic translation; not a target reading or certified modern pharmacology.

complete_selected_source.scope: Whole II.44.3 only. Together with RAW496 it would cover two of the five cabbage sections if a target extension were completed; RAW402/482’s all-five-section target gate is not declared met.

source_obligations: Previous lentil preparation should be like cabbage.
Lentil can cause both evacuation and checking of the belly.
Both cabbage and lentil prepared this way are named twice-boiled.
Apply the method to onion and leek, especially wild leek and garlic.
Extend to whatever else is desired to change toward the opposite of its original nature.
Remember above all that the twice-boiled material must touch neither air nor cold water.
After such exposure it no longer becomes properly soft, even if boiled for a very long time.
As already stated: have hot water ready, draw the same food from the former water and immediately transfer into the prepared hot water.

actual_new_content_if_bound.shared_portion: One prepared portion must retain its exposure history when it returns to the same replacement hot water and undergoes the second boiling. This would add a persistent restriction to the existing endpoint instruction without guaranteeing physical failure or success outside the historical claim.
actual_new_content_if_bound.two_causes: AIR contact and COLD_WATER contact are distinct events causing the same source-reported no-proper-softness restriction. Neither is silently identified with current coldness.
actual_new_content_if_bound.source_limits: No precise contact threshold, water temperature, duration, fraction, actual medical effect or unnamed new plant identity. A prior ordinary exposure of an uncooked plant is outside the modeled transfer scope.

serious_alternatives_if_future_binding_c.consequence: A portion exposed to air or cold water and then restored to hot replacement water still fails proper softening in the source claim, even with prolonged boiling.

Restored hot water would make exposed and clean inputs identical if present heat were the entire state; this loses the source’s history restriction. This is a meaningful source-model rival, but no actual target construction currently binds the contrast.
Replacing the earlier physical portion with a fresh one detaches the prohibited exposure from the later boiling. No such shift is silently permitted by the frozen water/food identities.
